input:
Labeled defect
- root cause: the wrapper now clears and reuses one statistics dict for every call instead of giving each call its own, so concurrent or nested calls of the same decorated function write into the same dict
- failure path: two threads (or two concurrent awaits of the async wrapper) call the same decorated function; the second call's stats.clear() wipes the first call's start_time and attempt_number, and both read a merged, wrong statistics view afterwards

Reviewer finding
- description: The shared statistics dict is cleared on every call. Concurrent coroutines of the same async-wrapped function share one dict, so each new call resets the stats of the calls already running.
- rationale: Trigger: `asyncio.gather` of several calls to the same retry-decorated coroutine. Each call executes `stats.clear()` and then writes to the same dict. Impact: `attempt_number` and `idle_for` are overwritten or reset across calls, so the statistics are wrong.
critique: The finding points to the same mechanism as the label: one statistics dict is cleared and reused on every call. Concurrent coroutines of the same wrapped function therefore overwrite each other's stats, such as attempt_number. The trigger (asyncio.gather) is one of the concurrent paths the label names.
